messages:
OncallBot: :warning: ALERT: gpu-pool eu-west-1/gpu-pool-2 at 92% util (queue depth 420/500). Low-priority route error rate +1.8%. Start time 1769554300. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/ops/alerts/1769554321

Sanjay: seeing a big bump from partner-integration-42 replays, looks like batched embeddings. spike started ~09:12UTC. Re-routing + admission control should help. @Katie any spare regional capacity?

Katie: no spare in eu-central. us-east has ~300 GPUs free but cross-region adds ~50ms median. Short-term plan: (1) admission control for low-priority routes, (2) spill a controlled % to us-east, (3) fallback to quantized model for spilled traffic.

Eli: cost FYI — spilling to us-east will incur egress + different pricing. Rough ballpark: spilling 10% of embeddings -> ~+1.8x per-token cost on that percent of traffic. fine short-term but track.

Alex: I'll prepare routing policy patch. Proposed policy snippet:
```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: eu-west-surge-spill
    match: route.tier == "low" && cluster.eu-west.queue_depth > 300
    actions:
      - set_spill_region: us-east-2
      - set_spill_pct: "auto"  # computed by controller
      - model_fallback:
          from: gptx-13b
          to: gptx-7b-q4
```
I'll open PR in a minute.

Maria: can we also reduce per-request concurrency for low-prio (concurrency cap 4 -> 2) to reduce KV cache pressure? admission control + spill is safer together. Remember fallback will slightly change embeddings; tag them.

Sanjay: agree do both. Also make spill percent auto-scale with queue depth so we don't overspill. Formula suggestion: `spill_pct = min(50, max(5, (queue_depth - 200)/6))` -> keeps it controlled.

Alex: adding the formula into controller. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-config/pull/842 (branch: surge-routing/eu-spill).

DeployBot: deploy started for routing-config@abc123 to staging (canary rollout). ETA ~2m. :rocket:

Katie: monitoring asks: add dashboard panels for `spill_pct`, `spill_region_egress_estimate`, and an alert if `spill_pct > 30% for 5m` or `eu-west queue_depth > 450`.

Maria: also add an eval hook that tags responses served by `gptx-7b-q4` fallback so downstream quality monitoring can separate them. We don't want silent regressions.

Sanjay: temporary SLO change: allow low-priority p95 latency drift to 60ms for 15m while we stabilize. ops-ok?

OncallBot: ACK. Incident declared: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-EU-SURGE. Updates will be posted here.

Alex: deploy finished. Canary reports: spill_pct started at 12% and ramped to 28% over 4m, queue depth reduced to 180, eu-west cpu/gpu pressure falling. No increase in high-priority errors.

Eli: cost projection based on current spill: extra ~$1.2k over next 24h if spill stays ~30%. tagging finance.

Katie: plan: keep spill policy live for 1h then re-evaluate and roll back if stable. Will set alert to auto-revert if we see >=2% error rise on high-priority.

Maria: added eval hook and tag shows ~0.6% drift in embedding similarity for fallback model. That's acceptable for low-prio but we'll watch.

Sanjay: thanks team. Patch looks good. Leave incident open until queue depth < 150 for 30m. :thumbsup:

OncallBot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Next update in 10m or on manual note.
